answer: Proof-of-replication binds each agent to a key-salted dataset replica verified via random Merkle challenges within strict response windows. Slow sequential encoding blocks cross-identity deduplication and live recomputation, forcing attackers to commit dedicated storage and disk I/O per identity, whether agents track raven calls, map grove plots, or mix pigment lots. However, adversaries renting cheap archival drives can still scale identities linearly at low marginal cost.
